A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SDPO research, with matching title, authors, and experimental domains. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D, support comparison; moved and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original SDPO experiments on DNA design, protein inverse folding, and language modeling, together with ablations and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original SDPO experiments across all three domains and adds results including a DNA training-data-size ablation.

M1.justification: The operational SDPO loss and implicit reward retain the same form (v1 Eqs. 13–14; v2 Eqs. 11–12), as do forward noising, masking weights, and iterative relabeling. Corrections to theoretical targets and derivations do not establish a changed training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same enhancer-design, PDB/Megascale protein, and UltraFeedback language coverage, with GSM8K, IFEval, and AlpacaEval 2.0 evaluation. The added DNA experiment uses smaller random subsets of the existing data, without introducing a different population or task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add D2-DPO and VRPO to both biological comparisons, retaining the previous comparators. Table 3 adds D2-DPO where v1 compared SDPO only with LLaDA-8B-Instruct. These additions substantially expand direct comparisons with other offline discrete-diffusion alignment methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds sequence entropy as a diversity metric in both biological evaluations. Appendix C.1 introduces first-stage training on random 25k and 50k DNA subsets, followed by the existing two relabeling stages. Previously documented training and language decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.1 and Table 7 test sensitivity to initial DNA training-data quantity. The existing beta, Monte Carlo sample-count, iterative-labeling, protein tradeoff, and language-response analyses are retained, including material renumbered within Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed averages with standard deviations in Tables 1–2 and retain the beta-sweep standard deviations and plotted error bars. Added result entries follow existing reporting practices; no changed experimental run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises SDPO's GSM8K score from 80.7 to 81.2 under unchanged documented settings and adds D2-DPO results. Tables 1–2 add comparator and entropy results while retaining their original biological scores; D2-DPO now leads DNA 3-mer correlation, 0.944 versus SDPO's 0.900. New Table 7 reports predicted activities of 5.56 and 6.02 for the 25k and 50k subsets, substantially expanding the reported evidence.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 and Appendix A.1 replace weighted conditional-mean trajectory rewards with log ratios of conditional exponential-reward expectations and substantially revise the proof. Section 4.3 and Appendix A.3 revise the importance-sampling derivation, while Proposition 4.3 and its asymptotic-unbiasedness proof are removed. The pairwise sigmoid algebra is corrected, and Appendix B.4 adds computational and memory complexity bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction update the headline GSM8K claim from 78.6-to-80.7 to 78.6-to-81.2 and explicitly frame SDPO as offline alignment. The principal contributions—stepwise decomposition, arbitrary-reward optimization, and an equivalence with a constructed trajectory objective—remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 now acknowledges that unbiased model-partition estimation requires conditional posterior sampling that is prohibitive offline, materially qualifying v1's consistency guarantee for the practical loss. Section 4.2 adds an interpretation of the revised transition rewards and their per-step supervision. The reward-model limitation is retained through relocation from Section 6 to Appendix D.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly documents computational and memory scaling, and Appendix C.1 specifies random subset selection followed by two established relabeling stages for the new ablation. Existing hyperparameter tables, GPU information, decoding settings, and code/data access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds D2-DPO, VRPO/LLaDA 1.5, d1, MMaDA, and Process Reinforcement through Implicit Rewards, and removes Song and Ermon's 2020 Improved Techniques citation. Related work now explicitly contrasts SDPO with pairwise offline and verification-based online discrete-diffusion alignment, within an otherwise retained discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory framing, method explanations, and experimental prose receive localized rewrites. The beta and sample-count discussions are reordered, the contents page becomes an appendix roadmap, and Section 6 becomes a conclusion with limitations moved to Appendix D. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an additional intermediate-step branch and revised reward labels. Tables 1–3 expand for new comparators and metrics, and a data-size table is added. Existing ablation plots and appendix result tables are largely retained with renumbering, resizing, and local page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central justification by revising the trajectory-reward construction and withdrawing v1's blanket asymptotic-unbiasedness guarantee (Theorem 4.1, Section 4.3, Appendix A). Close offline baselines, diversity metrics, and the data-size ablation also address important evaluation gaps. Some appendix equation inconsistencies remain, and new baseline settings and the GSM8K score revision are incompletely explained, but the gains in theoretical qualification and comparative evidence are substantial.
